findings.text: `assert hand in duty["next_command"]` compares `review_hand_dispatch_command(PROJECT, "r-refused")` against a `duty["next_command"]` that `_reflex_open_refusal` produced by calling the same builder (reckon/crew/obligations.py:1126). Both sides move together, so a regression in the builder's content — an empty string made it true vacuously, a wrong `--project` still matched — survives the assertion; it only reddens when the branch is replaced wholesale. Assert against an independent fragment such as `--role review` and the run id instead.

The fallback reads `pointer.get("review_dispatch")` as a literal where this module's established idiom is the owned constant `recovery.REVIEW_DISPATCH_FIELD` (obligations.py:630, :741, :803). A rename of the field would leave this reader silently stale — the recorded-refusal fallback would never fire — and only the one scenario in the test would notice. Use the constant.

justifications.durability: tests/test_every_delivery_the_reflex_owns_gets_its_review.py:299-317 drives a real sweep with a refusing launcher and asserts the injected refusal reaches both the pointer (line 303) and the duty (line 315), which gate-base-negative-control.log shows failing at the base revision; the lone weak link is the builder-self assertion at line 317.
justifications.evidence: gate-node-test-head.log records the three node cases 3 passed at revision 3c8873c61e and gate-base-negative-control.log records 2 failed, 1 passed at base 287b29e1, so the guard is shown to fire; ruff check and ruff format --check pass on all three changed files, but the done-when's 'importing files add no failure' arm is not recorded (both suite arms run only tests/test_staged_write_inventory.py) and no log names the all_debug partition.
justifications.fit: reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:2924 follows the surrounding lazy-import idiom and calls the owned reader; the naming and docstrings describe the mechanism, but obligations.py:1109 uses a field-name literal where the module's own constant exists.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/obligations.py:1106-1115 falls back to the refusal the run recorded at launch when the read-only predicate answers nothing, so an overdue duty for a launch-refused delivery now names that refusal and the hand-dispatch command instead of promising another sweep.
justifications.reuse: reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:2924 now calls the owned `_run_exit_record` (reckon/crew/recovery_liveness.py:1411) rather than re-parsing attempt-N-exit.json, resolving the duplication the prior review recorded; a repository-wide search for an existing hand-dispatch builder found only the new `review_hand_dispatch_command`, so it is the first owner.
justifications.scope_discipline: Every path in the delta (`reckon/crew/obligations.py`, `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py`, `tests/test_every_delivery_the_reflex_owns_gets_its_review.py`, the evidence fragment) is inside the source node's declared write paths listed in its manifest.
